PullRequest.Title: chat: fix CLI hook command validation

Fixes #343595.

## Changes

- Accept string-valued `command` alongside `bash`/`powershell` in the Copilot CLI hook JSON schema, including completion metadata.
- Update the missing-command diagnostic and preserve the existing command-field alternatives.
- Add a regression test for the command property and accepted alternatives.

The reported `version: 1` file already selects the CLI schema; its command-field requirement caused the squiggles. No harness-selection or runtime behavior changes are included.

The Local-format deprecation, default-snippet migration, and coordinated Configure Hooks changes are isolated in stacked draft #345634. This PR leaves the Local format and default snippet unchanged.

## Validation

- The focused branch retains the original command fix (`ed908b856cb`) and merges updated `main` in `145578ff518`; its diff against that main revision remains limited to the command schema and regression test.
- Standalone in-memory Ajv validation of the focused schema — passed 10 cases: command/bash/powershell, missing command, invalid command values, invalid type/timeout, Local compatibility, and the unchanged default snippet. A baseline regression check confirmed that the pre-fix schema rejects command-only input.
- `git diff --check ed908b856cb^ ed908b856cb` — passed.
- An independent full build/unit-test run of this focused branch was blocked during initial dependency bootstrap. After restoring public build dependencies, compilation, lint, hygiene, and 72 hook unit tests passed on stacked #345634, which includes this fix; those runs also include follow-up changes and are not an independent run of this branch.
- Live UI/CLI execution and broad type-checking were not run.

## Manual Check

1. Open the JSON repro in #343595 under `.github/hooks/`: command-only CLI hooks should have no missing-command diagnostic.
2. Remove the command or use a non-string value: validation should still reject the configuration.
3. Verify existing bash-only, powershell-only, and Local-format files remain accepted.

Draft for @roblourens and @aeschli.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup registers the hook JSON schema
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation constructs hookFileSchema and registerSchema stores it; the diff adds one small required-clause object and one property descriptor on this synchronous startup path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed O(1) additional objects, independent of workspace size, hook count, history, or session lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single registration during contribution initialization; the diff creates no queue, parallel work, or additional registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The schema is a module-level singleton registered once. Cold startup allocates the two added schema objects once; warm use reuses the registered schema with no new cache key or invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed lines only enlarge an existing in-memory schema by a constant amount.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact schema-registry initialization cost is not measured, but the added fixed-size literals are too small and non-scaling to establish a user-visible startup regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: constant startup allocation and registration work is negligible and introduces no expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit or open a versioned Copilot CLI hook JSON file and receive validation/completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing JSON language service applies hookFileSchema to the already-open document. For each hook command item, the change adds one constant-time anyOf required-field alternative and exposes one string property for completion.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Incremental CPU scales linearly with the number of hook command entries being validated, with one additional simple branch per entry; realistic effective cardinality is the commands in the active hook file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrency is introduced by the schema data. Existing document validation scheduling remains unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same registered schema object serves all matching files; the change adds no cache, cache miss, negative-cache state, or invalidation path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff and registration call show a pure in-memory schema change; runtime command parsing and schema association logic are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hook file sizes and validation frequency vary, but the incremental work is one simple required-key check per command item and does not add collection-wide copying, I/O, IPC, or unbounded state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the small per-command validation increment is necessary schema work and has no concrete mechanism for meaningful latency, CPU, or memory degradation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. The production change only adds constant-size JSON schema metadata; the test adds a one-time assertion. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, retention, concurrency, or repeated expensive-work regression is introduced, and the PR is not a performance-regression fix requiring blame.
